readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckLowerJointSmoothness.contDiffAt_lowerTerm_joint
readback.mathematical_statement: E is the fixed real three-dimensional Euclidean space ClosedSmoothModel 3. Bilin is E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R and Jet1 is E ->L[R] Bilin. Let BG = E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E, the space of continuous real bilinear E-valued maps, and let DBspace = E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E ->L[R] E, the space of continuous real trilinear E-valued maps. The revised literal type first locally selects the canonical Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedAddCommGroup and toNormedSpace structures on Jet1, BG, and DBspace, with both scalars explicitly R, source E, the displayed curried CLM targets, RingHom.id R, and the real scalar action. These selections retain each space's existing CLM operator norm and pointwise real module structure. They add no supplied hypothesis, replacement norm, topology, or extra data parameter. The usual normed products and original Bilin norm are retained. For every B in BG, DB in DBspace, G0 in Bilin, and J0 in Jet1, assume only G0.IsInvertible. This means G0, regarded as a continuous real-linear map E -> E dual, is the forward map of a continuous linear equivalence; it is not a symmetry or positive-definiteness premise. Then the actual Bilin-valued map p |-> DeTurckPrincipalIdentity.lowerTerm p.1.1 p.1.2 p.2.1 p.2.2 is C-infinity at ((B,DB),(G0,J0)), on the exact normed product (BG times DBspace) times (Bilin times Jet1). Thus all four arguments B,DB,G,J vary jointly, with the first pair containing background value and derivative data and the second pair containing metric value and first jet. The declaration does not freeze B and DB during the variation. C-infinity means ContDiffAt R at the ENat top injected into WithTop ENat, rather than the outer top regularity value. B and DB are arbitrary independent maps; no hypothesis requires DB to be the derivative of a background field with value B, or imposes symmetry, torsion, connection realization, or a metric relation. G0 need not be symmetric or positive-definite, and J0 need not be a realized or symmetric metric jet. The pinned lowerTerm is exactly (-2) smul ricciFirstBilin G J + J(fieldValue G J B) + G.comp(fieldFirstOperator G J B DB) + (G.flip.comp(fieldFirstOperator G J B DB)).flip. In vector slots v,w, its value is -2 * ricciFirst G J v w + J(fieldValue G J B) v w + G(fieldFirst G J B DB v) w + G v (fieldFirst G J B DB w). The finite-basis field and Ricci expressions use the existing actual connection G J u v = G.inverse(koszul J v u), retaining that argument order and the real CLM inverse from E dual to E. The total CLM inverse is zero off the invertible maps, but this smoothness conclusion is local at invertible G0 and does not claim global smoothness through singular bilinear forms. The output regularity concerns the whole actual continuous-bilinear-map-valued lowerTerm in its original operator-norm topology, rather than an existential lower witness or only scalar values at fixed v,w. There are no universe parameters, manifold, chart point, cutoff, time, Hoelder exponent, second metric jet, curvature, quantitative bound, flow, or linear operator package in this type. The conclusion gives joint finite-dimensional smoothness only. It does not itself supply an explicit Frechet derivative, a full finite-jet Q/DQ expression, differentiation of the principal inverse coefficient against a second jet, actual spatial coefficient fields or their covariance, a bounded global L, or a signed residual/contraction and physical flow. In particular the later principal contribution Da(G0)[dG] applied to H0 is not absent by virtue of this theorem; that contribution belongs to the separate full differential obligation.
